scholarly_control.author: Łukasz Popko
scholarly_control.title: Why Paul Was Not Wrong in Quoting Hosea 13:14
scholarly_control.consultation: Publisher PDF parsed body, printed499–501 and target table; not abstract-only. Native PDF/image layout could not be verified; shell downloads returned403, web screenshots yielded no inspectable image. No later pages, Hexaplar apparatus or plates claimed inspected.
scholarly_control.bounded_argument: Popko distinguishes possible questions, past-habitual, future and potential readings, while treating the context as negative. His comparison also preserves the ambiguity of whether Death is summoned or defeated. This challenges a grammar-only decision, rather than certifying a new Hebrew text.

root_reasoning.observation: Opening first-person imperfects lack explicit question particle or negation; they do not require assertions. Same-chapter where-form supports existing interrogative reading independently of Paul.
root_reasoning.strongest_for_N: Bound guilt, failed emergence at birth, withheld compassion, drying/plunder and Samaria's punishment form a sustained judgment sequence.
root_reasoning.strongest_for_R: Affirmative-looking paired imperfects and where-questions permit a rescue promise; Hosea11:8–9 and MT14:2–5 demonstrate reversal into mercy. Final relenting may concern an irrevocable rescue resolve.
root_reasoning.why_not_S: Possible modal nuance, but could introduces capacity or hypothetical possibility and weakens the deliberative question sequence.
root_reasoning.retained_limits: Questions' likely negative answer and summons function are contextual inferences. Do not add explicit NOT, imperatives, recovered letters or universal theology. Word/plague semantics, alternate I-will-be analysis and full versional apparatus remain separate questions.
root_reasoning.chronology: Early Greek reception informs attestation/interpretive range, not direct Hebrew speech-act priority; modest age preference does not reverse the contextual choice, and removing it leaves the working preference unchanged.

independent_hebrew_context_review.actual_verdict: The opening questions are grammatically valid and fit the immediate judgment context better. Declaratives remain a serious alternative.
independent_hebrew_context_review.scope: Read-only contextual argument, not a manuscript or publication review

candidate_assessment.actual_verdict: Frozen assessment: select candidate N as a qualified working preference; preserve R as the serious alternative. S is defensible but weaker than N on the contextual speech act.
candidate_assessment.blindness_statement: I did not read the target YAML, new candidate/comparison records, or identity maps.

assessments.label: S
assessments.meaning: Fits judgment as rescue possibility foreclosed by withheld compassion.
assessments.additions: Could supplies a particular modal nuance not independently fixed by morphology.
assessments.literary_and_readability: Clear but weakens confrontational questions; may sound like unfinished offer.

assessments.label: N
assessments.meaning: Best local fit with sustained judgment and withheld compassion.
assessments.additions: Question punctuation interprets speech act; no Hebrew negative or imperative added.
assessments.ambiguity: Promise R must remain visible; later where-questions can summon or taunt.
assessments.literary_and_readability: Parallel questions retain rhetorical force; shall slightly elevated but intelligible.

assessments.label: R
assessments.meaning: Grammatically straightforward rescue promise and victory taunt; local hidden compassion and renewed destruction create tension.
assessments.additions: No added lexeme, but morphology must not be asserted to compel it.
assessments.ambiguity: Abrupt mercy reversal possible; alternative referent for final clause needed.

candidate_assessment.strongest_contrary_argument: Mercy reversals in Hosea11 and14 are genuine; they preserve R as live, but do not outweigh the immediate judgment sequence under the shared Compassion wording.

reopen: A discriminating Hebrew witness/apparatus reading, stronger local discourse explanation of the saving-promise/final-clause transition, or independently evaluated versional punctuation/interpretation may reopen the preference. Extra tokens or model agreement alone do not.
